notes:
1. Brief 2026-10-10-microsoft-decision-1-decision-model, body says "Microsoft's Decision-1, based on Qwen3.5-9B, handles classifications, evaluations and routing decisions, The Decoder reports." Source (The Decoder): "According to Microsoft, it handles classifications, evaluations, and routing decisions". The claim is Microsoft's, not The Decoder's. Fix: "Microsoft says Decision-1, based on Qwen3.5-9B, handles classifications, evaluations and routing decisions."
2. Brief 2026-10-10-microsoft-decision-1-decision-model, body says "Microsoft says it is the most accurate model across 36 benchmarks." Source: "Microsoft says it's the most accurate model tested across 36 benchmarks covering nearly 150,000 questions." Dropping "tested" widens the claim to all models. Fix: "Microsoft says it is the most accurate model tested across 36 benchmarks."
(The 2026-10-11 note text itself is clear: sections 1-4 and the dek match their sources. Only the Microsoft brief, which the note connects, still carries the two errors flagged in the previous review and left unchanged.)
